newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Royal&Sun puts bought for dividend play.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Royal&Sun puts bought for dividend play.

text.p: The main UK stock option deals on Friday concerned buying put options in insurer Royal & Sun Alliance and in British Airways, dealers said.
Shares in the insurer Royal & Sun Alliance will go ex-dividend on Monday and the options may have been purchased to lock-in profits.
The deal was to buy 2,000 October 515 puts at 108p against the purchase of 2.134 million shares at 415p making a net debit of 523p.
Once the shares have gone ex-dividend the puts can be exercised to sell stock at 515p.
After collecting the dividend -- of 6.5p net of basic tax or 8.125p gross -- they deal is assured of an overall profit.
By 1340 GMT, the underlying shares had slipped 2-1/2p to 415p.
For British Airways 1,000 January 600 puts were bought at 40p against buying 6,600 shares at 574p.
In general, if the shares fall, the puts can be exercised in order to limit the losses.
But if the shares rise, profits will come from the shareholding less the cost of the puts.
British Airways shares were up a sharp 18-1/2p at 580p.

Elsewhere, a calendar call spread was established in British Petroleum involving the sale of 500 October 600 calls at 76p and the purchase of 500 January 600 calls at 82p -- effectively buying medium dated calls cheaply.
In British Gas the biggest deal was the sale of 750 December 180 puts at 5p. Another trader bought 580 lots at 6p.
British Gas shares fell 6p to 187p while those of BP were added 2-1/2p to 679-1/2p.
